evidence.quote: The lawyer went across to his desk, and returned with a small newspaper cutting, which he handed to Jane.
“When I came across this paragraph,” resumed the lawyer, “my problem was solved.

adjudications.reason: The revision opens directly with “When I came across this paragraph”, and nothing in 027.revision shows a cutting first. Chapter 026.revision ends on Sir James's accusation, not on a document. The plan lists the New York cutting as essential, and 028 relies on 'the paragraph in the New York paper'. The disfigured-body detail is useful but not required, so it is left out to stay within budget.

evidence.quote: “Can’t you? I can. So can young Beresford, by his actions.
I threatened Julius with the revolver, because I wanted Tuppence to repeat that to Sir James

adjudications.reason: Tuppence's surviving line raises the rescue only. Sir James then cites 'young Beresford, by his actions', meaning the hold-up, which he has not been told about in 026.revision or 027.revision. In 028, Tommy says he threatened Julius so that Tuppence would repeat it to Sir James. That telling is what is now missing.

evidence.quote: Then Julius Hersheimmer dashes up and rescues you in true melodramatic style.

adjudications.reason: 'Him' follows directly after 'So can young Beresford, by his actions', so the referent is clear enough. 'Rescues you in true melodramatic style' and 'Bullets fly--but don’t hit anybody' still convey the staging. This is a legitimate compression.

evidence.quote: “Nothing until we’ve been to the house in Soho.”

adjudications.reason: The drive is an optional tradeoff. 'Nothing until we’ve been to the house in Soho' and the police-watch dialogue make the transition clear. The reveal still punctures Tuppence's 'We’ve succeeded'.

evidence.quote: Even now Tuppence could almost swear it moved--as though _some one_ was behind it.

adjudications.reason: The required fancy clue, the curtain that seems to move, is kept, along with the insistent feeling and the 'faint sound behind him'. The footstep is an extra clue, and cutting it is acceptable.

evidence.quote: I slipped the two stuck-together pages with their precious enclosure between the picture and its backing

adjudications.reason: In 026.revision, Jane has just described slipping the stuck-together magazine pages behind the Marguerite backing. 'Frayed inner edges' therefore has a recent antecedent, and the recovery stays clear.

evidence.quote: The treaty? It is in the hands of Mr. Brown. So no one will think of searching the pockets of Sir James Peel Edgerton!
with a wealth of detail! So no one will think

adjudications.reason: Without the middle step, 'So' in protected V5 follows the wounded-survivor line and makes no logical sense. The source premise is that the treaty is attributed to Brown. The fix restores that sentence and nothing else.

remaining_concerns: The net restoration is about 40 words against a target of 36, so a slight overshoot is accepted rather than cutting meaning.
The cutting sentence is condensed from source paragraph 1 rather than restored verbatim.
